title: Abba Bira’ah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman finds him mentioned only once, in [Menachot 93b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.93b.12): “It was taught: Abba Bira’ah son of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says,” etc. [Heilprin, under Bira’ah](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=710&lang=en), is uncertain whether he was the son of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov or spoke in his name. Hyman firmly proposes a small correction in the books, following Dikdukei Soferim: “for Abba Bira’ah recited a baraita.” Hyman explains that Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov also arranged baraitot, as cited in the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 1, chapter 6. In Hyman’s explanation, this Abba Bira’ah brought one baraita from the baraitot of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov. Bira’ah is a town-name, as in [Megillah 4a](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.4a.10), Ulla Bira’ah, and Rashi explains: from Biri.[^1]

notes.text: Menachot gives the compact form be-Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov. Heilprin considers a son, a transmitter, and someone of Rabbi Eliezer’s school. Hyman instead reads the line as Abba Bira’ah reciting a baraita. In the separate Megillah passage, [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Megillah.4a.10.1) glosses Ulla Bira’ah as from Biri.
